title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics with Δ+2 colours
formal: Do absolute constants C,c>0 exist such that, for every finite simple n-vertex graph G with maximum degree Δ and every integer q≥Δ+2, the single-vertex heat-bath Glauber chain on proper q-colourings has total-variation mixing time t_mix(1/4)≤Cn^c?
definitions: Let n≥1 and Ω={σ:V(G)→[q] : σ(u)≠σ(v) for every edge uv}. Colours are labelled; unused colours are allowed. At each discrete step choose v uniformly from V(G), then choose a colour uniformly from [q]\{σ(u):u∈N(v)} and assign it to v, leaving all other vertices unchanged. The current colour is among the available choices. Let P be this transition matrix and π the uniform distribution on Ω. Define t_mix(1/4)=min{t∈Z_{≥0}: max_{σ∈Ω} (1/2)Σ_{τ∈Ω}|P^t(σ,τ)−π(τ)|≤1/4}. This counts individual vertex updates, not sweeps or bit operations. The constants C,c must be independent of n, Δ, q and G. The initial proper colouring is arbitrary, and the graph has no girth, treewidth or randomness promise. This card fixes a uniform polynomial bound across degrees, rather than leaving the exponent’s parameter dependence implicit.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated uniform bound for this particular Markov chain, or prove that no universal polynomial bounds its worst-initial-state mixing time over the specified graphs and palettes. A polynomial-time sampler using another chain does not by itself answer the question. A counterexample must concern q≥Δ+2; frozen colourings with fewer colours, or a failure of one coupling argument, are not refutations.
context:
A proper colouring is easy to construct greedily with this many colours. Sampling one nearly uniformly is a different task: a deterministic rule can strongly favour a small part of the solution space. Glauber dynamics is an appealing candidate because every update uses only a vertex and its neighbours, yet repeated local changes must reproduce the global distribution. The inherited paper states the conjecture and proves it for particular graph classes.

The threshold Δ+2 has a concrete role. On a clique with Δ+1 vertices and exactly Δ+1 colours, every vertex sees all other colours in its neighbourhood. No vertex can change colour, so each proper colouring is a separate absorbing state. With at least Δ+2 colours, the single-vertex chain is irreducible on every graph and converges to the uniform distribution. The unresolved issue is how long this convergence takes.

Connectivity of the recolouring graph is insufficient to control that time. A walk may need to cross a narrow passage between two large collections of colourings. Even short paths between every pair do not show that a random walk finds the appropriate passages often enough. The card therefore asks for a distributional guarantee from the worst starting colouring, rather than a bound on the number of recolourings in an intelligently chosen path.

The update convention matters when comparing sources. A second standard version proposes a colour uniformly from the entire palette and rejects it if a neighbour uses it. This is the Metropolis version used in several cited papers. Its off-diagonal transition probabilities and the heat-bath probabilities differ by a factor between 1 and q/(q−Δ). That factor is at most 1+Δ/2 in the present range, so the distinction is relevant to sharp runtime statements but does not create an exponential gap between their polynomial-mixing questions.

The early general-graph milestones were Jerrum’s q>2Δ regime and Vigoda’s improvement to roughly 11Δ/6. The latter used a flip chain that interchanges two colours on a small connected bichromatic component, followed by a comparison with single-vertex dynamics. Chen and coauthors subsequently crossed the 11/6 threshold by a small constant improvement. The 2026 ICALP paper retains Δ+2 as a conjecture, including its Glauber-dynamics version.

Carlson–Vigoda’s October 2024 revision gives a substantial further improvement. Theorem 1.1 assumes Δ≥125 and q≥1.809Δ and proves O(n log n) mixing for the flip chain. Comparison gives polynomial mixing for Glauber dynamics in that regime. Their optimal O(n log n) Glauber corollary has a constant depending on Δ and q; it is stated for fixed parameters. The headline coefficient should therefore not be read as an unrestricted optimal-time theorem for all degrees.

Graph structure can bring the colour threshold much closer to the target. Heinrich proves n^{O(tw(G)^3)} mixing with q≥Δ+2, so bounded treewidth is covered even when maximum degree is unbounded. For chordal graphs, the proved regime instead uses q≥(1+ε)(Δ+1) for a fixed positive ε. Letting treewidth grow with n, or substituting ε that shrinks with Δ, does not give the uniform statement in this card.

There was further progress during 2026. Jain–Mizgerd–Vigoda prove O_δ(n log n) mixing for the Metropolis chain when q≥(1+δ)Δ, Δ is sufficiently large in terms of fixed δ>0, and the graph has sufficiently large girth. Their August 27 revision improves the required girth from eleven to seven. This is stronger than the original April abstract, but still excludes general graphs and does not establish additive slack of only two colours.

Chen–Liu’s August 26 preprint reaches girth at least five in the same fixed-relative-slack regime for heat-bath dynamics. Its Theorem 1 proves spectral gap Ω_δ(1/n) and mixing time O_δ(n² log q+n log(1/ε)); the sharper O_δ(n log n) consequence requires degree bounded in terms of δ. Both the girth restriction and the dependence on δ matter. Taking δ=2/Δ is not justified by a theorem that first fixes δ and then requires sufficiently large Δ.

The other inherited 2026 source studies an additional constraint: prescribed colour-class sizes. Such a condition changes the sample space, and a single-vertex update generally cannot preserve it. Its algorithms for equitable or mildly skewed colourings therefore address a separate sampling problem. They provide useful context for why global constraints complicate local sampling, while explicitly leaving the unconstrained Δ+2 conjecture open.

This is fundamental because it tests whether the basic local sampler remains efficient throughout the universally ergodic range. A proof would connect a simple combinatorial availability condition with global probabilistic convergence. A negative answer would identify an obstruction to efficient local sampling that survives despite spare colours at every vertex and connectivity of the entire state space.
why: A central boundary question for Markov-chain sampling: does the simplest local recolouring process mix efficiently whenever the universal ergodicity threshold is met?

importance.reason: A longstanding general-graph conjecture linking local algorithms, approximate counting and spin systems; recent near-threshold results still require structural restrictions.

progress.text: Jerrum proves rapid mixing above the 2Δ colour threshold.
Vigoda reaches the 11Δ/6 regime using flip dynamics and comparison to Glauber dynamics.
Chen and coauthors improve the 11/6 coefficient by an absolute positive constant.
Heinrich proves the Δ+2 result for bounded treewidth and a fixed relative-slack result for chordal graphs.
Carlson–Vigoda v2: Δ≥125 and q≥1.809Δ suffice for optimal flip mixing; Glauber mixing follows with the parameter qualifications stated in the card.
The ICALP fixed-colour-class-size paper still states general Δ+2 sampling and Glauber mixing as conjectures.
Chen–Liu preprint gives rapid heat-bath mixing at girth at least five, for fixed relative slack and sufficiently large degree.
Jain–Mizgerd–Vigoda v2 improves its girth condition from eleven to seven for optimal Metropolis mixing at fixed relative slack.
